doc.title: Ashley Keating and Allan Whitworth Interview, 1963-03-22

title: The alto player and the young tuba player
summary: Keating and Allen discuss alto saxophonist Earl Batiste, who had played with R&B bands, Keating's dislike of saxophone, and the very young tuba player.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Uh, he seemed a very good musician. Uh, being a dyed in the wool, uh, Bunk Johnson and Lewis fan, uh, to be quite frank, no saxophone, uh, really moves me. Although, uh, having heard Manuel Paul, uh, play tenor, I found that quite interesting. Uh, but this, uh, lad was obviously a good musician. There's no two ways about that. Again, he played with a fairly strong vibrato. Uh, I would have liked to have heard him on some other instrument. I think you suggested to him, he might perhaps like to play a soprano or a clarinet. Uh, I'd agree with you there. I think he, uh, probably would be much, uh,

easier to listen to on one of those instruments. Well, they said he'd been with various bands like Bull Moose Jackson and Ray Charles, and I hadn't expected anything which was generally in the New Orleans idiom that much out of somebody who'd been with those people. No, No, he seemed, he seemed to be familiar with what they were doing. He was conversing with,
there's nothing sure of. Yeah, and, and, uh, it's strange how those people pop out of, out of nowhere. He would have been relatively young too, I'd say, wouldn't he, about 25 or so?
The tuba player they seemed to like, and he's, what, something like 16 or 17.
